title: Marble Maze Tilt with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D marble maze game using Three.js. The maze environment is loaded from 'collision-world.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (e.g., three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). The marble rolls on top of the loaded collision world which acts as the maze surface.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 15, 15) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0 and castShadow enabled.
- Set the renderer background to #1a1a2e. Enable shadows on the renderer.
- Load 'collision-world.glb' using GLTFLoader. Once loaded, center it at the origin and scale it so it fits roughly within a 20x20 unit area. Enable receiveShadow on all meshes in the model. Store a reference to the loaded model.
- Create a marble (SphereGeometry, radius 0.4) with a shiny metallic MeshStandardMaterial (color: #e94560, metalness: 0.8, roughness: 0.2). Place it at position (0, 2, 0) initially. Enable castShadow.
- Add an OrbitControls instance but disable it by default (controls.enabled = false) so arrow keys are free.

## Physics (Simple Custom Physics)
- Implement simple physics: the marble has velocity {x, y, z} and is affected by gravity (y -= 9.8 * dt).
- The maze platform (collision world) can be tilted by the player using arrow keys. Track tiltX and tiltZ angles (in radians, clamped to [-0.15, 0.15]).
- Arrow Up/Down tilts the platform around the X-axis (tiltX += or -= 0.005 per frame while held). Arrow Left/Right tilts around the Z-axis (tiltZ += or -= 0.005 per frame while held).
- Apply the tilt to the collision world model's rotation: model.rotation.x = tiltX, model.rotation.z = tiltZ.
- The marble accelerates due to gravity projected onto the tilted surface: apply force proportional to sin(tiltX) in Z direction and sin(tiltZ) in X direction, scaled by 8.0.
- Apply friction (multiply velocity.x and velocity.z by 0.98 each frame).
- Simple ground collision: if marble.position.y < 0.4 (marble radius), set y=0.4 and velocity.y = 0. This is a simplified collision.
- If marble falls below y = -10, reset marble to (0, 2, 0) with zero velocity. Increment a fallCount.

## Undo/Redo System
- Every 1 second, automatically save a snapshot of the marble state: {position: {x,y,z}, velocity: {x,y,z}, tiltX, tiltZ}.
- Store snapshots in an array (max 60 snapshots, FIFO). Maintain an undoIndex pointer.
- Press 'U' key to undo: restore the previous snapshot (decrement undoIndex). The marble position, velocity, and tilt all revert.
- Press 'R' key to redo: restore the next snapshot (increment undoIndex). Only works if undo was performed.
- When a new snapshot is saved after an undo, discard all snapshots after the current undoIndex (standard undo/redo behavior).
- Display undo/redo availability in the HUD.

## HUD / UI
- Create a DOM overlay div with id='hud' at top-left showing:
  - 'Tilt X: {tiltX.toFixed(3)}' and 'Tilt Z: {tiltZ.toFixed(3)}'
  - 'Marble Pos: (x, y, z)' rounded to 2 decimals
  - 'Speed: {speed.toFixed(2)}' where speed = magnitude of velocity vector
  - 'Falls: {fallCount}'
  - 'Snapshots: {number} | Index: {undoIndex}'
  - 'Undo (U): {available}' and 'Redo (R): {available}' showing 'Yes' or 'No'
- Add two HTML buttons with ids 'btn-undo' and 'btn-redo' that also trigger undo/redo.
- Add a 'Reset' button with id 'btn-reset' that resets marble to start, clears velocity, resets tilts to 0, and clears snapshot history.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - marblePos: {x, y, z} (marble world position)
  - marbleVel: {x, y, z} (marble velocity)
  - speed: number (velocity magnitude)
  - tiltX: number
  - tiltZ: number
  - fallCount: number
  - snapshotCount: number
  - undoIndex: number
  - canUndo: boolean
  - canRedo: boolean
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true once GLB is loaded)
  - timeElapsed: number (seconds since start)

Make sure the animation loop runs at 60fps target using requestAnimationFrame with a delta time calculation (capped at 1/30 to avoid large jumps).
physics_constraints: Gravity is 9.8 m/s² downward. Tilt angles clamped to [-0.15, 0.15] radians. Friction coefficient 0.98 per frame. Marble radius 0.4. Surface force = 8.0 * sin(tilt). Marble resets if y < -10. Velocity and position must remain NaN-free at all times.
